correctness.rationale: De Cataldo proves \(\sum_{n\ge0}\chi_c(S^{[n]})q^n=\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{-\chi_c(S)}\). Formal logarithmic differentiation gives \(n a_n=e\sum_{j=1}^n\sigma_1(j)a_{n-j}\), hence \(e\mid n a_n\); cancelling \(\gcd(|e|,n)\) proves the claimed divisor. The \(e=0\) case is immediate from the product. An independent product-expansion checker verifies the identities over positive and negative Euler characteristics.

value.rationale: The theorem converts a single geometric invariant \(\chi_c(S)\) into an infinite family of exact arithmetic constraints on all Hilbert schemes of points. It is uniform over every smooth complex algebraic surface in the product-formula scope, gives nontrivial prime-adic information even when exact Euler characteristics are large, and produces a sharp reusable divisor such as \(24/\gcd(24,n)\) for the hyperkähler K3 Hilbert-scheme series. This is a structural consequence rather than a finite table or a normalization check.
